analysis: This batch contains only documentation and changelog changes: changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md (added), docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (lines 3 and 318-322) and docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 3 and 252-259). No source code is in the supplied evidence. The docs describe a provider-side behavior change: SSD prefix-cache complete-checkpoint import now builds destinations from zeroed host buffers, without MLX evalLock evaluation or fencing, so staging does not wait behind another request's prefill. Relevant threat IDs are T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007), A-001 and T-010/T-029 (availability). Security-relevant claims to verify in the code, which is not supplied: (1) the import plan charges the largest zeroed host buffer as stage scratch against ProcessMemoryLedger/Admission before allocation (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift). Host buffers are outside the MLX allocator, so an under-charge could cause memory-pressure DoS. (2) Skipping the eval/fence for destinations built from host bytes must not weaken the completion and retirement barriers or let a destination be used before the copy completes. (3) DBK3 authentication, HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping, TTL and KEK bindings should be unchanged. The docs state the SSD read path claims bounded host buffers before I/O and that native destinations remain under Admission. The docs do not change the T-041 posture. None of these claims can be confirmed from the docs alone, so the code-side changes (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and related) need review by whoever has that source. No findings are raised on docs-only evidence.
